title: Regiment and Ledger
premise: In the port city of Vellacourt, 1848, Theo Delacroix keeps her late father's print shop alive by cutting typefaces under her brother's name while revolution smolders in the streets. When an injured stranger leaves a child at her door with a ledger of names and orders to forget his face, Theo discovers the book implicates her brother Marcel, now an officer enforcing the regime he once swore to overthrow. As the crackdown tightens, the ledger becomes both evidence and death sentence for everyone named in it. In the end, Theo must decide who boards the last ship out on the morning tide — she gives the berth to the child, stays behind to print the truth herself, and lets Marcel face the tribunal rather than save him.
about_author: Ivo Galloway is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment before turning to fiction. Galloway writes historical novels about ordinary people caught between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Theo Delacroix cuts type by lamplight in her father's old shop, measuring her life in ems and picas while rumors of uprising pass through the customers. Her brother Marcel visits in uniform, uneasy, warning her to keep the press cold. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, love strained by politics.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Night
chapters.summary: A bloodied stranger pounds on the shutter at midnight, leaves a swaddled child and a leather ledger, and says only 'forget my face' before vanishing into curfew streets. Theo hides him from a patrol, then opens the book. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; no going back.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: By candlelight Theo reads coded entries — payments, betrayals, executions ordered — and finds Marcel's signature beside three names she recognizes as neighbors who disappeared. The child, a girl of four called only Bird, sleeps through it all. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold shock.

chapters.title: Marcel's Uniform
chapters.summary: Marcel arrives for Sunday dinner; Theo watches him lie smoothly about the disappearances while Bird plays at his boots. He nearly sees the ledger; Theo deflects. Flashback to their father teaching them both the press. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: grief for the brother she remembers.

chapters.title: The Compositor's Union
chapters.summary: Theo seeks out Odile Ferrand, an old printer's widow who runs an underground network of pamphleteers, hoping to decode the ledger's cipher. Odile agrees but warns that knowledge is a debt that gets collected. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: cautious alliance, first taste of resistance.

chapters.title: Bird Learns the Shop
chapters.summary: A quieter chapter: Bird becomes part of the shop's rhythm, sorting type scraps, and Theo confronts what guardianship means for a woman with no standing and no money. A customer reports soldiers asking questions about the print shop. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by encroaching danger.

chapters.title: The Man Who Forgot His Face
chapters.summary: The stranger returns, wounded worse, and reveals himself as Luc Arnaud, a clerk who copied the ledger to expose Colonel Vassey's profiteering off executed prisoners' estates. He begs Theo to hide it until the fleet sails. POV: Luc. Emotional beat: guilt and desperation; trust extended under duress.

chapters.title: Vassey's Men
chapters.summary: Colonel Vassey himself visits the shop, courteous and venomous, buying a printed broadside as pretext to search. He mentions Marcel by name — his protégé. Theo realizes Marcel is complicit not just by signature but by ambition. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror masked as civility.

chapters.title: Cipher and Confession
chapters.summary: Odile cracks the cipher: the final pages name every official in the pay of Vassey's ring, including the date the fleet departs with smuggled gold. Marcel's last entry is dated three days ago. Theo copies the key onto movable type, hiding it in plain sight. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing into plan.

chapters.title: Brother Against Brother
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Marcel privately with the ledger. He doesn't deny it; he argues survival, family, the futility of martyrs. She asks him to testify against Vassey; he refuses and warns her the shop will burn if she prints. POV: alternating Theo and Marcel. Emotional beat: heartbreak without reconciliation.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Soldiers ransack the shop hunting Luc. Theo has hidden him in the type cellar; Bird, coached or instinctive, distracts a sergeant by reciting letters. They find nothing, but the shop is wrecked and Theo is marked. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: white-knuckle suspense, cost made real.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Odile reveals the network is compromised — one of her own couriers sold names to Vassey. To distribute the ledger's truth they must print openly, once, fast, and accept the consequences. Theo volunteers her press. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: sacrifice accepted communally.

chapters.title: Setting the Type
chapters.summary: Theo composes the exposé overnight, each line of type a small act of treason, while Luc dictates corrections and Bird sleeps in the paper bin. Marcel sends a covert note: sail tomorrow or be arrested with the rest. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: sacred focus; craft as conscience.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Copies
chapters.summary: Dawn run: the network floods the markets, barracks gates, and harbor taverns with the printed ledger excerpts. The city ignites — strikes, barricades, soldiers refusing orders. Vassey declares martial law and puts a price on the printer's head. POV: Luc. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into open war.

chapters.title: The Berth Question
chapters.summary: Luc secures passage on the morning tide ship: exactly one berth left, plus coin. Theo, Marcel (now facing arrest for the exposed ledger), and Bird cannot all go. Luc urges Theo to take it; she refuses to choose yet. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: Marcel's Choice
chapters.summary: Marcel comes to the ruined shop at night, out of uniform, offering to surrender the rest of Vassey's records if Theo takes the berth and takes him with her story — testimony instead of exile. It is the closest thing to repentance he can offer. POV: Marcel. Emotional beat: shame reaching for redemption.

chapters.title: Vassey Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Vassey arrests Odile and shells the printers' quarter. Theo learns the tribunal will try Marcel at dawn — before the tide. Saving him means abandoning the public testimony that could topple the whole ring. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: fury and clarity arriving together.

chapters.title: The Tribunal at Dawn
chapters.summary: Theo storms the hearing with the original ledger and Marcel's surrendered records, reading names aloud until the chamber erupts. Officers defect mid-session; Vassey's command collapses. Marcel testifies, damning himself willingly. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: justice seized outside the law's good graces.

chapters.title: Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the quay, with the tide turning, Theo makes her choice: Bird boards with Luc as guardian, carrying the ledger copy abroad where it can never be burned. Marcel, bound for prison and likely the scaffold, presses his compositor's hand-tool into hers. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: grief and peace in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Ship Sails
chapters.summary: From the breakwater Theo watches the ship shrink toward open water, Bird's small hand raised at the rail. The city behind her burns in patches and sings in others; the revolution holds, barely. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: release, loneliness, unshaken conviction.

chapters.title: Reset the Form
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Odile freed in the general amnesty, the tribunal dissolved into a civilian court, Vassey fled and named in absentia. Theo reopens the shop, Marcel's sentence commuted to labor he serves quietly nearby. She hangs Bird's sorted type scraps above the door. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: mending without forgetting.

chapters.title: The First Impression
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Theo prints the shop's new broadsheet — truth, weekly, signed with her own name at last, no longer her brother's or her father's. A letter arrives from Luc with Bird's drawing of the sea. She locks the forme, pulls the lever, and the press speaks. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: identity claimed; the story ends on ink and morning light.
